target_customer: Urban Indian households in Delhi NCR and online buyers who want organic staples with traceable sourcing
problem: Consumers cannot tell where organic food comes from or how much farmers earn, and small organic farmers lose margin to traders.
business_model: Direct to consumer organic grocery brand sourcing from farmer collectives with capped margins (60 percent to farmers, 30 percent operations, 10 percent overheads, per the YC page)

founders.name: Shubham Bansal
previous_startups: Leap Club (the company's earlier name per YC page and aggregators)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, which describes him as co-founder at Leap Club.

founders.name: Divish Gupta
founders.background_notes: Company site says he has worked in farming, food and sustainability since 2015 and volunteered in Auroville for two years.

founders.name: Raj
founders.background_notes: Named only as Raj on the company site, which says he was a filmmaker before building conscious organisations; one aggregator gives a surname that I did not verify.

competitors.name: Earthy Tales
competitors.what: Sources organic produce directly from farmers and says it removes middlemen

competitors.name: Zama Organics
competitors.what: Mumbai organic food brand sourcing from a reported network of over 50,000 farmers
competitors.traction_then: Network of over 50,000 farmers per YourStory

technical_complexity.rationale: A D2C grocery brand needs ecommerce and supply chain operations, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Relationships with five farmer collectives and a transparency story help, but other organic brands source from farmers too.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents acting against it.

market_need_then: YourStory estimated the Indian organic food market at about 1 billion dollars in 2020 growing at 20 to 25 percent a year; IMARC and EMR gave 815 and 849.5 million dollars for 2020.

branding.domain_note: Uses swadesiway.com, exact name .com; history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, conversational and playful, greeting visitors with Hi, friend and using phrases like Take the Swadesi Way

branding.brand_signature: Radical transparency about price split and farmer earnings (60 percent to farmers)

rebrands.why: Not found; a Wefunder page title in search results shows Swadesi Way formerly Leap Club

branding.community_and_virality: A crowdfunding campaign listing about 68 investors was seen in a search snippet; no merch or press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear mission-led positioning on the site but no press, community or brand coverage found.

pivots.from: Leap Club (earlier company name under which it joined YC W21)

outcome_analysis: Swadesi Way joined YC Winter 2021, originally under the name Leap Club, and now sells organic staples sourced from five farmer collectives with a stated 60 percent share to farmers. It is listed as Active with 9 staff. Public funding is limited to YC money and a small crowdfunding campaign seen only in aggregator snippets, and no exit or failure was found, so the outcome is unproven rather than clearly good or bad.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (Extruct, Dealroom) say a seed of about 125K led by YC, and a Wefunder snippet says about 105,567 dollars from 68 investors closing September 2021, but the Wefunder page returned 403 and nothing was cross-checked, so no round is recorded. Founding year conflicts (2019, 2020, 2021). The legal entity is Twig Labs Private Limited per the company site. No outcome news found. The YC page and the company site name different cofounders, so all three are recorded with sources. Update: the company was formerly Leap Club (leap.club, YC W21 per Wefunder page title and Dealroom). Press reports an 810K pre-Series A (YourStory, Oct 2021, recorded as pre_seed, led by Enzia Ventures, Kunal Shah and users) and a 1M round (late Nov or Dec 2022, led by Enzia Ventures; Inc42 dates it 2022-11-30). Press also mentions a 380K seed in July 2020, not recorded because no source page was opened. Inc42 totals 2.26M over 4 rounds as of Dec 2022 and CB Insights 2.15M, so rounds may be missing. The Wefunder 105,567 dollars (Sept 2021) likely sits inside the 810K round, so it is not recorded separately. The 125K Extruct and Dealroom figure conflicts and is not recorded. Inc42 reports leap.club halted operations (date not confirmed); exit not changed.
